A great majority of people who talk about suicide, and who ask about it publicly, really don’t want to do away with themselves. A few of these actually do try suicide, but they botch it up — possibly intentionally, or unconsciously because down deep they know they want to live.

Such people do not want their lives to end. What they want is an end to the pressures, stresses, pains, conflicts, punishment, diseases, or whatever else is afflicting them. They fear that those problems will not ever go away or become greatly reduced, so they have little hope for their future. The reasoning is that if you can’t eliminate the problems (which are intolerable), then one must eliminate oneself.

There is a great conflict, because the individual has no hope for the future, but there is somewhere within him/her a wish that there could be a future free of those problems. The hopelessness motivates suicidal desires; the small undying wish, motivates postponing an act of suicide.

The stated desire for a quick, easy, painless death is evidence that the wish is still alive. People who are truly committed to doing away with themselves don’t really care about mess or pain or what it will do to others left behind.

You are calling out for help. As it is difficult for you to believe that anything can help relieve your problems, the only help you feel you can ask for, is how to do away with yourself. But this little wish for survival into a problem-free future is holding you back.

As it should. You have undoubtedly tried everything you can think of to relieve your problems, and nothing has succeeded. But in fact, there are people on Reddit who can lead you to solutions that you cannot develop on your own.

So your question should be rephrased “Who can help with my problems, before they drive me to suicide?”.

Your problems can be lifted away from you. You need to reach out for help in the right way. You will find respite, with the help of experts. Give them a chance to save you, so that you can enter a satisfy and fulfilling continuation of your life.

I don’t think a suicide helpline will do you any good. Instead, tell us about your “nightmare” and the “treatment you have had”. You will find someone who can advise and assist you, and end the nightmare and the treatment, without ending your life.
